qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 3 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
qualitative.summary: Omar spends time in Manshiyat Naser, Cairo's garbage collectors' (Zabbaleen) neighbourhood, where families collect, sort and recycle the city's waste, and he sets out to replace a prejudice with respect. The film opens on a sensory cold open ('careful, careful', trash in his face, 'We're creating the garbage, not them') and is guided by one local man in a blue cap who reappears as a recurring companion. The middle combines sorting rooms lit by single tubes, rooftop storage, pigs and the Coptic Christian context, and Omar's small participations (sorting, a haircut). The last third moves to a recycling and crafts NGO (Association for the Protection of the Environment), where women turn waste into paper, quilts and can-tab bags, then ends on an embrace with the guide and a 'Made in Egypt' line.
qualitative.hook_analysis: Spoken cold open from 0.1 s. Omar walks into an alley toward camera (0:00) with the guide and reacts to the smell and sight ('I'm not sure coming here was a good idea'). Quick frames of sorting, trucks and rooftop bags (0:10-1:49) are cut against direct questions to workers ('Are you not wearing any gloves?'). The moral reframe arrives inside the hook ('We're creating the garbage, not them', 'You're the ones keeping Cairo clean'). Replay heat is highest at 0:00-0:14 and again at 1:10-1:24 (an elder by a mural, hands sorting).
qualitative.narrative_arc: Sensory cold open (0:00-1:51) -> drone and map of the neighbourhood, with Omar naming his own prejudice (1:58-2:58) -> meeting the guide and his family business (3:08-3:57) -> dark sorting rooms and long-time workers (4:07-6:45) -> NGO first glimpse and aerials (6:55-7:44) -> street life: elders, barber, shops, children (7:54-10:52) -> Omar sorts, rooftop storage (11:01-11:41) -> recycling chain: grinding, flakes, pellets (12:01-14:00) -> religion and pigs: Coptic context, pig pens (14:09-16:17) -> NGO workshop: paper, weaving, quilts, can-tab bags (16:57-21:14) -> farewell with guide, final to-camera (21:23-22:33) -> logo.
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Tight handheld in narrow alleys with a wide lens; Omar is often framed from below against the buildings (0:00, 2:48, 8:53). Low-key interiors where a single fluorescent tube is the light source (4:27-4:56, 6:25). Close character portraits of elders and children with shallow depth (1:39, 7:54, 10:22, 10:42). Straight-down drones over the dense rooftops as punctuation (7:34, 16:57, 21:53) and oblique city aerials (1:58, 2:58, 7:14, 22:42). Some workers' faces appear blurred or turned away (0:30, 1:29). Exact moves are not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Neutral white balance, dark overall (brightness 0.30, 15% low-key frames), with a muted khaki and grey-green palette. The colour comes from the blue, green and pink garbage bags rather than from a grade push. Exteriors have hard, dusty backlight (8:43, 21:33-21:43). The NGO workshop brightens up and becomes more colourful (teal and red quilts, 17:07-21:14), so the grade lifts as the story turns hopeful.
qualitative.sound_and_music: The most continuously talked-through of the six: speech coverage 0.73, non-speech only 5.5%, longest speech-free run 22 s (the outro). 132 wpm, 85 questions and a high second-person rate (0.034): Omar repeatedly addresses the viewer and the workers directly ('Like you, when I first heard...'). Talking-to-camera stretches at 2:43-4:02 and 11:26-12:35 are flagged by the profile. The audio itself was not analysed.
what_to_borrow: Name the audience's likely prejudice yourself, early, then let the film dismantle it
Keep one local guide as a recurring companion and pay off the relationship at the end with an embrace
Use straight-down drones over dense rooftops to show scale between claustrophobic alley scenes
Follow the material chain physically (bag -> sorting -> grinding -> pellets -> crafts) so the 'respect' argument is shown, not told
Let the grade and setting brighten as the story turns from hardship to dignity
what_to_avoid_copying: Disgust reactions in the hook ('Oh, god!', trash in the face) risk 'poverty tourism'; this film balances them quickly with respect, so keep that balance
Some workers appear blurred or turned away: get consent and plan the coverage rather than hiding people in the edit
Talk-wall density (73% speech) leaves little room to breathe; plan more visual pauses

observations.name: sensory cold open
observations.description: Omar walks into an alley toward camera with the guide (0:00-0:20), sorting women (0:30), trucks (0:39-0:49), trash flying at him (0:59). 'Careful, careful' and 'not sure coming here was a good idea'. Highest replay heat at 0:00-0:14.

observations.name: moral reframe inside the hook
observations.description: 'We're creating the garbage, not them' (0:49), then context on pigs and Christian workers (1:08-1:17) over an elder by a religious mural (1:19) and hands sorting (1:29); replay peak at 1:10-1:24.

observations.name: aerial and map establishing
observations.description: Oblique drone over the dense brick neighbourhood (1:58), a loaded pickup (2:08), a satellite map with the area traced in white inside the vintage frame (2:18).

observations.name: naming the viewer's prejudice
observations.description: Talking-to-camera run: Omar framed through a vehicle window (2:48), a second aerial (2:58), and the line 'Like you, when I first heard about this neighborhood' (2:58).

observations.name: meeting the recurring guide
observations.description: Omar and the guide in a blue cap sit on bags in his sorting space (3:08-3:47), ending on a cheek-to-cheek two-shot (3:47); the guide returns at 12:20-12:50 and 22:03-22:13.

observations.name: low-key sorting rooms
observations.description: Single-tube-lit interiors with long-time workers and subtitles (4:27-4:56, '40 years?'), bag contents (5:06), a woman sorting beside Omar (5:36-5:55), Omar reacting (6:15-6:35); replay peak at 6:30-6:44.

observations.name: NGO glimpse and top-down drone
observations.description: The Association for the Protection of the Environment sign (7:05), a city aerial (7:14), Omar walking with the founder (7:24), a straight-down rooftop drone (7:34).

observations.name: street portraits and barber
observations.description: An elder close-up (7:54), Omar laughing with him under the mural (8:04), the founder's portrait (8:33), a barber shop (9:03-9:13, 'How's the haircut?'), a laughing elder (10:22), a schoolboy (10:42).

observations.name: Omar sorts, then the rooftop
observations.description: Omar sorting bags with a worker (11:11), climbing up (11:21), then on a rooftop above the city with stored garbage (11:31-11:41).

observations.name: recycling-chain macro
observations.description: Plastic flakes in water (13:10), Omar at the shredder (13:20), a grinder spraying pellets (13:49), with the narration on pellets going 'straight to factories'.

observations.name: Coptic context
observations.description: A poster of Coptic saints on a wall (14:09), with the subtitle line that most people in this work are Christians (14:29).

observations.name: pigs (replay peak)
observations.description: Pigs in a pen (15:18), a heap of organic waste (15:28), a close-up of a pig (16:07); replay peak at 15:19-15:33.

observations.name: NGO workshop: dignity through craft
observations.description: Paper making from waste (17:26-18:06), quilts and weaving (18:26-18:45), a founder interview in front of a geometric quilt (18:55, 20:44), can-tab bags (19:15), with the line 'From poverty to life' (20:19).

observations.name: backlit return and embrace
observations.description: Dusty backlit alley shots (21:33-21:43), a top-down drone (21:53), the guide and Omar walking (22:03), and an arm-around embrace (22:13).

observations.name: final to-camera and logo
observations.description: Omar's closing to-camera in a sorting yard (22:23-22:33), with 'Made in Egypt' (22:22); the logo over an oblique city aerial (22:42), then black logo cards (22:52-23:02).

limitations: Frames are YouTube storyboard previews (YouTube storyboard 320x180, one frame every 9.9s); fine detail, exact cuts, transitions and camera movement are not measured.
Shot types use face/sky/edge heuristics on low-resolution frames - treat as approximate.
